Led by a local expert, the experience is set to be a lively introduction to the people, places and ideas that have shaped one of the UK’s most influential cities The tour will begin at Manchester Central Library, that impossible to miss, grand circular landmark on St Peter’s Square. The neoclassical design has made it one of the city’s most-loved buildings, holding thousands of stories in its walls and on its shelves. The square itself ha From here, the tour takes you through the city’s heart, down the colourful streets of the Gay Village and the calming Sackville Gardens. It is here that you will see the monuments that honour Manchester’s role in the fight for equality and the city’s pioneering LGBTQ+ community a This guided tour is filled with monuments and tales from many moons ago. The Medieval Quarter is the perfect place to soak in all that history. It is here where you will see the oldest public library in the English-speaking world, Chetham’s Library . Housed in a beautiful sandsto During all this walking, your guide will point out local street art, hidden corners and stories you’d easily miss on your own. Tales of suffragettes, reformers, musicians and everyday Mancunians who’ve all left their mark on the city in their own way

Jonathan Scofield’s tour Sleazy, Sinister and Haunted Manchester takes you deep into the shadows, unearthing a side of the city that rarely sees the light of day The tour begins at Manchester Cathedral which in itself sets the tone for the tour that follows. Like, really big. They’re expanding beyond Freight Island and into the cavernous Depot Mayfield to create the We Are Football Festival, a huge fan park experience with space for a staggering 13,000 fans. Expect giant anti-glare screens, a stadium-style sound system, pyrotechnics, CO2 cannons, DJs, giveaways, Sky Sports presenters, England legends, food, bars and the sort of atmosphere you’ll still be talking about if this really is the year that it comes home. Instead, the changes have happened quietly, almost without people noticing. A different route to work. A decision to leave the car at home once or twice a week. A later These aren’t dramatic lifestyle overhauls. They’re small decisions, made for practical reasons, that have slowly reshaped everyday travel As work patterns continue to evolve and people become more conscious of both time and wellbeing, Manchester’s commuters are proving that lasting change often happens one habit at a time Whether it was a quick trip to the supermarket, a visit to the gym or a short journey to meet friends, reaching for the car keys required very little thought. Convenience almost always won For journeys of only a couple of miles, many people now pause before starting the engine. Fuel costs, parking charges and traffic all play a part, but they aren’t the whole story. People are becoming more aware that some short journeys can actually feel easier without the car

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Fire crews tackling a moorland fire have been inundated with drinks, food and treats collected by a cricket club where two of its members are firefighters Micklehurst Cricket Club, in Mossley, Greater Manchester, has become a mini-depot where donations of food and drinks have been collected for firefighters who have been tackling the blaze near Dove Stone reservoir, since Saturday "It's not just the club, it is the local community that has rallied," said Matt Barton, who has been one of those making deliveries to the fire crews three miles away He added: "The response has been incredible - people have been so generous." RECOM Solutions has opened a 2500 sq metre warehouse and office facility at Trafford Park as part of a six-figure investment in its RECOM Fire Solutions division. The new hub consolidates several smaller North West sites into a single location, increasing storage capacity, improving logistics and strengthening stock management. The investment also includes an expanded vehicle fleet to support projects nationwide. Sarah Leadbetter, head of passive fire protection at RECOM Solutions, said: “The opening of our new North West distribution hub is a major milestone for RECOM Fire Solutions. “It creates greater efficiency through a centralised location, increases storage capacity and improves stock management. “Trafford Park is an ideal location, as it’s highly accessible and close to our group headquarters in Salford Quays. “It provides us with a strong base for our next phase of expansion and will contribute to reducing our carbon footprint as a business.” RECOM Fire Solutions delivers passive fire protection services across the education, healthcare, residential, defence and facilities management sectors, with work including fire stopping, fire door installation and remediation, compartmentation surveys and fire curtain installations. The Trafford Park opening follows the launch of a Birmingham base earlier this year , extending the division’s reach across the Midlands, M6 corridor and South West. evidence_packet.evidence_text: musicMagpie’s Steve Oliver follows Pep in announcing exit Posted on July 3, 2026 by Chris Maguire musicMagpie’s Steve Oliver follows Pep in announcing exit musicMagpie founder and lifelong Man City fan Steve Oliver has announced he’ll be leaving the company and handing the reins to Jonathan Miller Share: Founders Steve Oliver has announced his exit from musicMagpie. Oliver famously co-founded the business with Walter Gleeson from his Stockport garage in 2007 and will leave his role as managing director in September. After first revealing his intention at the company’s annual conference, he took to LinkedIn to reveal his near-20-year journey with the company will come to an end on September 30. Originally set up as the ‘lazy man’s eBay’, musicMagpie allowed people to trade in their CDs, DVDs and games for cash. With developments in technology, it pivoted towards phones and gadgets and floated on the London Stock Exchange’s junior AIM market in April 2021 with a share price of 193p. AO buys musicMagpie: ‘Life was pretty tough as a standalone PLC’ That represented a market capitalisation of £208m. However, musicMagpie’s share price dropped to almost 5p in 2024 before fellow London-listed company AO stepped in with an offer of 9.07p in cash per share, valuing the business at just under £10m . Just like his hero, former Man City manager Pep Guardiola, he said it felt like the right time to leave. Oliver said: “My greatest single pride at Magpie has always been the people …. more so than our cumulative £2bn of gross income in our history so far, more so than the little business that started in my garage in Hazel Grove becoming the biggest seller in the world in the history of eBay and Amazon and more so than paying out well over £1/2bn pounds in tax-free cash to our customers

Welcome to CONEXEN Manchester – A warm and welcoming community for professionals and founders in biopharma, life sciences, and health tech in Manchester! Here, we invite you to join us for an informal and friendly gathering where connections are made, knowledge is shared, and friendships are formed. Come with an open heart and a willingness to “listen” rather than “sell.”

​​We will be hosting our Manchester event at the amazing space of Cloud 23 Cocktail Bar. It is a casual setting where we can come together, exchange greetings, engage in conversation, and simply enjoy a pleasant time.

​​Picture this as more than just an event, it’s a life sciences community gathering. Our focus is on providing you with an opportunity to meet fellow professionals and founders in a relaxed and amiable environment. We’ll share conversations over delicious food and drinks, and leave with a sense of excitement and a pocketful of new contacts and ideas.

​​Join us for an evening surrounded by incredible people, and let’s make it a night to remember. Looking forward to sharing good company and creating memorable connections!

​Theme: The Forces Reshaping Work & Culture in Life Sciences.

Join a focused discussion led by Paul Bradley-Law on the forces redefining culture in a hybrid world. Our panellists will explore how hybrid working, evolving HR trends, leadership style, and a multi-generational workforce are reshaping how organisations operate, alongside the growing influence of AI in the workplace.

We’ll examine how trust is built through clarity and candour in uncertain times—without defaulting to micromanagement—and how to address “proximity bias” to ensure fair visibility, recognition, and opportunity across distributed teams.

Join peers shaping the North-West Life Sciences ecosystem and driving the region’s growing influence.

​Moderator: Paul Bradley-Law (Founder, The Great People Machine)

​Panelists:

  • Ike Cooke, Business Growth & Commercialisation Manager, LYVA Labs

  • Julia Buckler, Senior Director, Site Head, Qiagen

​The format of the night:

  • ​18:00 Doors open – drinks, networking and meeting great people.

  • ​18:30 Talks start

  • ​19:15 Drinks, food and networking.

  • ​20:30 End of the night – you leave with new contacts and fresh ideas.

​​Venue: Cloud 23 Cocktail Bar – The Manchester Deansgate Hotel, 303 Deansgate, Manchester M3 4LQ, United Kingdom.

This event is proudly supported by Nexa Life Sciences and Kadans Science Partner, hosted by Kadans Science Partner.

​

​And finally…

​This is a ticketed event. Food and drinks for the night are included.

​Please let your colleagues and industry friends know about us, we hope to build it into a great resource for the ecosystem over the coming months and years. Attendance will be taken at this event. If you register but don’t show up, this has a knock-on effect on event arrangements. If it happens 3 times, we may need to reconsider your participation. This is simply a measure to allow appropriate respect to the organisers, speakers, sponsors, and your fellow Conexers.

​See you there!

​Ashley, Julia, and Sajid
Manchester Organisers

​Tickets FAQs: https:/www.conexen.net/faq

The new facility will provide CAF with Increased overhaul capacity, ensuring improved turnaround times, and enhancing fleet reliability whilst reducing asset downtime. Initially the facility will provide work for around 30 employees, many recruited locally, however, this number is expected to double as work on the site ramps up. It will also serve as a training centre for new CAF employees. It will be supported by CAF’s Central Stores Facility in Stockport through a just-in-time supply model, ensuring parts and materials are delivered as required to maintain efficient operations and minimise inventory holding at the new Lowry Park site. Drawing on emerging frameworks including ISO/IEC 42001, the NIST AI Risk Management Framework, and the EU AI Act, this session will provide practical guidance on establishing governance for both internally developed AI solutions and the use of public AI platforms. Join us for a practical discussion on how to build effective AI governance that balances innovation with trust, accountability and risk management. Once owned by the late Jimmy 'The Weed' Donnelly , a member of Manchester's notorious Quality Street Gang, in 2016 the pub became the focus of a high-profile mur Mr Joyce, then 29, of Gorton , was last seen at the Pollard Street pub in September 1999. Seventeen years later, police dug up the cellar of the Bank of England after being tipped off that Mr Joyce's body was buried there It came after GMP received 'credible' information he had been killed during a fight. But, the Manchester Evening News revealed, the force had been informed three years earlier about the possibility that Mr Joyce's body was in the pub - and not acted Nothing was found during the two week police excavation at the property. The dad-of-one's disappearance remains unsolved and the case is with GMP's cold case unit

Comments News Edward Barnes Local Democracy Reporter Oldham councillors have been warned the local authority could soon be breaking the law, as a top boss issues a warning. Elected members have been told they have two weeks to come up with someone to lead them or things could get much worse After no one was elected as Oldham Council’s leader on July 1, the local authority is still in limbo with officers continuing to use emergency powers just to keep services running . Key political decisions cannot be made and multiple meetings have been cancelled as a result The recent local elections on May 5 left no party with a majority or even a third of seats in the council chamber. Bids to lead the council put forward by Labour , Reform UK, and an alliance of different parties have all been rejected with everyone blaming each other for the dead Some progress has been made but the council is not able to function normally without a political leadership to drive the organisation forward. One councillor suggested to the Manchester Evening News the situation inside the council is now akin to ‘a poisoned lake’ View 2 Images Councillors meeting on July 1 (Image: Copyright Unknown)

A search of Miah’s property found the ID card, plus two sergeant patches, police trousers, a police belt and a laptop bag Inquiries revealed the newly single father of one had previously quit Greater Manchester Police (GMP) ahead of him being fired after he was caught driving his BMW 3-series car without insurance outside a police station - then lying about it in a bid to avoid the blame After his resignation, he then failed to hand in most of his police-issue items due to a ''mistake.'' At Tameside Magistrates' Court , Miah from Highfield Street, Oldham , pleaded guilty to impersonating a police officer and unlawfully possessing articles of police uniform

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Fires Fire service warns more smoke to hit Greater Manchester today amid huge wildfires Easterly winds are carrying the smoke plumes across our region amid the Dovestone and Tintwistle wildfires Comments News Ashlie Blakey Live and breaking news repor Fire chiefs have warned that more smoke will billow over Greater Manchester over the next 24 hours amid two huge wildfires near the region Two major wildfires, one at Dovestone and Swineshaw and one at Tintwistle, are continuing to rage on this weekend. It is more than a week since the moorland fire began at Dovestone, while crews have been battling the Tintwistle fire for more than three weeks The fires have sent huge plumes of smoke over Greater Manchester and beyond. The Derbyshire Fire and Rescue Service (DFRS) last night (Saturday) said a controlled burn would be carried out at Tintwistle This is set to cause an increase in smoke over the next 24 hours, the fire service said. Easterly winds are carrying the smoke plumes across our region The controlled burn allows crews to 'remove fuel that would otherwise allow the fires spread further'. People affected by smoke have been urged to keep their windows and doors shut

It came, jurors heard, amid a feud between the Moston based 'M40' gang and the Rochdale and Oldham outfit Representing the Danger (RTD). M40 gang members became overwhelmed and fled, it was said Mr Soyoye was injured in the earlier fight, jurors heard. evidence_packet.evidence_text: Greater Manchester Police GMP to get £22m for extra police in Jewish communities in wake of Heaton Park synagogue attack The money will go towards putting on extra officers around schools, community centres and synagogues News Damon Wilkinson Reporter Greater Manchester Police is to get an extra £22m to pay for more police in Jewish communities in the wake of the Heaton Park synagogue terror attack The money will go towards putting on extra officers around schools, community centres and synagogues in areas such as Prestwich and Broughton. It will also fund specialist and plain-clothes officers trained to identify suspicious behaviour Announcing the move today (Monday) as part of a nationwide £250m boost to police budgets for tackling antisemitism , the Prime Minister said it was a ' step-change in protection and policing so Jewish communities can live and celebrate their faith free from fear' Crime and Policing Minister, Sarah Jones, added: "After a series of appalling attacks against Jewish communities, the difficult decision was made to raise the threat level to Severe. My thoughts remain with the victims of these vile attacks "Today we are going further and providing record funding to help keep Jewish people in Manchester safe, supporting visible policing and protection around synagogues, schools and community centres. We will do everything in our power to rid society of the evil of antisemitism."

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Fires Greater Manchester's new air quality map shows moor fires' devastating impact in every borough as urgent health warning issued Only one area of Greater Manchester is now classed as having 'good' air quality Smoke billows over Greater Manchester It comes as dozens of firefighters are continuing to tackle two major wildfires on the moors near Dovestone Reservoir in Oldham and on Tintwistle Moor near Glossop. FOLLOW LIVE UPDATES HERE Firefighters from Greater Manchester Fire and Rescue Service were first called to Dovestone on Saturday night . A major incident was declared on Monday afternoon and, on Tuesday, they said 70 firefighters were still tackling the blaze A woman, aged 20, was arrested on suspicion of arson over the Dovestone wildfire. Shania Care-Slede, of Market Street , Hyde , has now been charged and has appeared in court The wildfire at Tintwistle, above Woodhead Road in Glossop, first broke out nearly three weeks ago amid the heatwave on June 24. Derbyshire Fire and Rescue Service declared a major incident as the blaze raged on Both fires are sending huge plumes of smoke across our region and beyond - with new air quality maps showing the deteriorating impact the fires are having across Greater Manchester

Paul Sharpe is awaiting his fate after abducting a 15-year-old girl at knifepoint, forcing her into his car and sexually The 56-year-old, from Stockport , has admitted his latest sickening crimes and will be sentenced later this year. But it is not the first the Sharpe has committed an abhorrent crime against a female in Greater Manchester Back in October 2000, Sharpe murdered a Bolton woman who he was in a relationship with. The pair had struck up a romance after she listened to Sharpe on a radio show he hosted at the time on Tower FM, under his alias Paul Shaw Sharpe fatally strangled the 28-year-old mum, a beauty therapy student at Bolton College, after she threatened to break up with him. He went on the run, but three days later handed himself in, telling officers he had 'flipped' after the relationship appeared to be reaching an end Sharpe, then of Wellington Road, Bury, was handed a life sentence at Manchester Crown Court the following March. The judge, Mr Justice Penry-Davey, told him: "You deprived her of her life and her son of his mother."

Questions are being asked over delays in the building of more than 270 homes in the Salford district of Ordsall in a scheme being managed by the council's development company Dérive The plans, which include 100 much-needed affordable houses in what is still one of the city's most deprived areas, were first approved in March 2024. It was hoped the 'vibrant, inclusive' estate's first residents would have moved in by now But more than two years on not a single brick has been laid. The two plots off Robert Hall Street were once home to a school and a shopping precinct But they have been fenced off and left to stand empty ever since they cleared of trees and groundworks carried out in the summer of 2024. And in the meantime residents say the site is becoming more and more of an eyesore

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Fires Major road closure update after car bursts into flames and spreads to moorland The A628 Woodhead Pass remains shut after the crash on Thursday News Ashlie Blakey Live and breaking news reporter 08:38, 18 Jul 2026 View 2 Images The scene of the b A major road over moorland near Greater Manchester will remain shut until at least Monday following a car fire The car burst into flames on a stretch of the A628 Woodhead Pass between the A57 at Hollingworth and A616 at Flouch on Thursday afternoon (July 16). Shocking photos from the scene showed a black car completely engulfed in a blaze Smoke and flames could be seen billowing from the vehicle, which had left the road and crashed on adjacent moorland just after 1.30pm. The fire then spread to adjacent moorland, a South Yorkshire Fire and Rescue Service spokesperson said The crash came amid the major moorland fire in Tintwistle, above Woodhead Road, which first broke out round three weeks ago . The blaze has spread over the moorland and burned an area the size of at least 350 football pitches After the car crash on the A628, the road was closed off in both directions. National Highways has now confirmed in an update that the closure is expected to remain in place until at least Monday morning

Marcus Smith was pronounced dead at the remote farm on Eccles Road, Whaley Bridge, in the early hours of May 1 2024 The budding footballer, who played for local club Chapel Town FC had sustained a fatal gunshot wound and died from his injuries. A second 19-year-old, who also suffered gunshot wounds on the same evening, was found nearby and treated in hospital before being discharged Police and forensics remained in attendance at the farm for a number of days following the shooting. Drone shots showed two police vans and four other unmarked vehicles parked beside the two-story farm near Whaley Bridge The homeowner on the property, a man aged in his 50s, was arrested on suspicion of murder and taken into police custody. It was revealed at the time that the shooting had happened during a suspected burglary incident He was then released on police bail as investigations into the incident continued. It was then confirmed on Tuesday (July 11), more than two years after the incident, that no further action was to be taken against him and he was released from bail

But for decades the Collier Street baths in Greengate has been an empty decaying shell Now it could have a new lease of life as Mackie Mayor style food hall which is housed in another historic building - Manchester's former Smithfield Market Hall on the edge of the Northern Quarter The listed former baths, built in 1855, is situated in the Colliers Yard development which was the former medieval heart of Salford. Renaker secured planning permission to build three tower blocks in 2020 on condition that the baths were restored The Cortland block was completed in October 2023 - a 50-storey tower with 559 rental apartments. Thomas O’Rourke was found guilty of 31 offences against his victims between the 1970s and 1990s which started when some of them were children Greater Manchester Police said the offences occurred at various points across different decades in areas including Middleton and Blackley . His victims have now spoken out about the abuse they faced at the hands of the now 74-year-old Thomas O’Rourke, of Newton Heath was jailed for 26 years at Bolton Crown Court on Monday (July 6) after he was found guilty of rape, sexual assault and indecent assault. Leading detectives on the case said he will spend the rest of his days in prison The first survivor came forward in 2019 to police, reporting offences that occurred when they were a child. Further survivors were then uncovered who supported the investigation and brought O'Rourke to justice During her victim impact statement read to court, one survivor said: "I stand here today to finish giving that child you tried to destroy, her voice, and end all the hurt you caused. As Ms Rigby went to cross the road, the toucan pedestrian crossing was on red and the traffic light was on green for vehicles, she was hit by Read's Vauxhall Insignia She was left with catastrophic injuries that resulted in her immediate death, Manchester's Minshull Street Crown Court heard During a two-week trial earlier this year, police told the court that if Read, 33, had been travelling the speed limit, he never would have hit Ms Rigby. He was found guilty of causing death by careless driving and was today handed a suspended jail term Robert Smith prosecuting, said that shortly after midnight, Ms Rigby left her home and walked along the A580, a dual carriageway governed by a 50mph limit. Ms Mutch said the mother-of-one died from the 'toxic effects' She said there was no evidence of any kind of any intention on her part to take her own life - saying she was planning for Christmas and wrapping presents The inquest heard Ms Allen-Gyves, from Sale , Trafford , had totally transformed her life after an addiction and was taking prescribed medication to treat opiod use disorder, as well as prescribed medication for ADHD. A 'significant level' of an over-the-counter medication was al Ms Mutch said it was likely Ms Allen-Gyves, who also taught geography at the school and was a member of its senior leadership team, was trying to 'manage down' her prescription at the same time as 'self-medicating' to try to sleep

And it all brutally came home for Carol Knight when she found out her car had been firebombed - and the culprits were never found Carol’s car was firebombed in May 2023 in Derker, Oldham , in what she believes was a targeted attack. At the time, her daughter, Angela Cosgrove, was running for re-election as a councillor for the St James ward which covers the area - and Carol believes it was linked to that But despite the damage, Carol says ‘nothing seemed to get done’ as a result. “The sad thing is people were afraid of opening up," she said. "People were frightened about things coming back onto them “I didn’t feel any reassurance. Nothing whatsoever that the police were going to look into it. A lot of people will have known because we had been here for 70 odd years and people said if they do not look after you, what will they do to us? “That to me told me and my husband if they can’t do anything, why can I be bothered? That to me said something needed to be desperately done.”

evidence_packet.evidence_text: That’s according to England talisman Harry Kane with the striking superstars set to face off tonight in a thrilling World Cup quarter-final. Haaland will lead the line for Norway with Kane set to skipper England in the 22:00 (UK) knockout clash at Miami Stadium. It’s a battle between two of the world’s most prodigious frontmen with not only progress to the last four up for grabs but also the competition’s Golden Boot in the balance with Kane on six and Haaland on seven behind only Argentina’s Lionel Messi and France’s Kylian Mbappe on eight in the fight for the prestigious individual gong. Heading into this evening’s hotly-anticipated encounter, Kane waxed lyrical about his opposite number. “Erling has been incredible,” said Kane. “Look at his goal scoring record. And physically, he’s a machine, he’s a beast. “His finishing is at another level and his goalscoring record speaks for itself. “I respect him a lot as a player and as a fellow professional. “I’m obviously hoping he has a quiet day. His performances speak for themselves. He’s a fantastic player.” The performances of both prolific forwards have led to comparisons and naturally questions of which player is better. It’s a discussion Kane refused to get drawn into primarily because he believes they’re different type of strikers. “It’s an impossible one for me to answer’” he added. “I think we are completely different players. I know we are both seen as strikers but we are almost two different positions if I’m totally honest.” City Magazine: World Cup special available now! Featuring Rayan Cherki, Erling Haaland, Omar Marmoush and a greatest ever World Cup Manchester Best XI - get reading now!
